headline: Meta is seeking $20 billion to $25 billion in bond sale for AI spending
body: Meta is seeking to raise between $20 billion and $25 billion in a bond sale on Tuesday as it ramps up spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure, models and services. The debt sale is expected to be two-thirds in U.S. dollars and one-third in euros, according to people familiar with the matter. The sale comes days after S&P Global Ratings revised Meta's outlook to negative, citing "uncertainty" about its capex spending and negative free cash flow.
note: Meta's latest quarter posted negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, and full-year capex will come in between $135 billion and $145 billion.

evidence.text: Meta is seeking to raise between $20 billion and $25 billion in a bond sale on Tuesday as the company ramps up its spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure along with AI models and services.
The debt sale is expected to be two-thirds in U.S. dollars and one-third in euros, according to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be named because the details are private.
Meta's bond sale comes days after S&P Global Ratings revised the company's outlook from AA- stable to AA- negative, citing "uncertainty" about its hefty capex spending and negative free cash flow.

In its third-quarter earnings report last month, the Facebook parent revealed that its full-year capex will come in between $135 billion to $145 billion, representing a $5 billion increase to the low end of its previous guidance.
Meta posted negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion for its latest quarter, joining Alphabet and Amazon in reporting a negative figure.
